title: Specified inverse and finite-Tor bounds for a shifted line under site comparison
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], so $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, $n\geq1$, and $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $T$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with no absolute separatedness assumption. Write $V_T=\nu_T^*$ for exact derived comparison from the small etale to the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on both sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], with ordinary derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor, def-weil-derived-tensor]. Let $L$ be an etale sheaf of $A$-modules which is locally isomorphic to $A_T$, and let $m\in\mathbf Z$. Put $L^\vee=\mathcal Hom_A(L,A_T)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom].

The sheaves $L,L^\vee,V_TL,V_TL^\vee$ are constructible [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and the last two are pro-etale locally isomorphic to $A_T$. The specified evaluations, given on a local basis $e$ and dual basis $e^\vee$ by $(ae)\otimes(be^\vee)\mapsto ab$, induce isomorphisms in the derived categories
$$L[m]\otimes_A^LL^\vee[-m]\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T,\qquad L^\vee[-m]\otimes_A^LL[m]\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T.$$
Under the canonical tensor and unit comparisons for $V_T$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], these are precisely the corresponding evaluation isomorphisms for $V_TL[m]$ and $V_TL^\vee[-m]$. Both complexes lie in $D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], with Tor intervals $[-m,-m]$ and $[m,m]$, respectively. For every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ of Tor amplitude $[a,b]$, their tensors with $K$ remain bounded constructible and have Tor amplitude $[a-m,b-m]$ and $[a+m,b+m]$, respectively. The analogous bounds hold on the etale site, with Tor amplitude as in [def-kun-tor-amplitude].

source.place: First paragraph, sentences “omega_f[-2d] is a locally constant free rank-one sheaf” and “In particular it is tensor-invertible”; inherited proof Step 4, including flatness, specified evaluation, comparison and finite-Tor inverse

proof.text: Apply the ringed-site line-evaluation lemma on the etale site with $R=A_T$ and $P=L$. It identifies the given sheaf $L^\vee$ as another locally free rank-one sheaf, gives both flatness assertions, and gives the specified evaluation and its inverse, with $e((ae)\otimes(be^\vee))=ab$. The reverse-order evaluation is the ordinary sheaf symmetry followed by this map. Its formula is also multiplication. Because $A$ is finite, the stalks of both locally constant sheaves are finite; the one-stratum partition $T=T$ therefore makes both constructible by the etale definition. No stratification theorem or separatedness assumption is used.

source.place: Tags 0B8Q (lemma-invertible-is-locally-free-rank-1), 0B8N (lemma-invertible), applied to the given trivializations

proof.text: For comparison, use the inclusion of etale schemes into the pro-etale site. It preserves finite limits and coverings. The comparison-exactness lemma identifies the pulled coefficient ring with $A_T$, so its module pullback is the exact inverse-image functor in the item. Apply the finite-locally-free dual-pullback theorem to the rank-one trivializations of $L$. The pulled trivializing covering is a covering on the target site, and its comparison identifies $V_TL^\vee$ with $\mathcal Hom_A(V_TL,A_T)$, sending the pulled dual basis to the dual of the pulled basis. In particular both $V_TL$ and $V_TL^\vee$ are pro-etale locally $A_T$. The ringed-site line lemma on that site gives their flatness and evaluation isomorphisms. Their locally constant finite values and the one-stratum partition give pro-etale constructibility.

source.place: Tags 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom), 0FNY (example-dual); Tags 0B8Q and 0B8N; comparison uses Tag 099R in proetale.tex

proof.text: On either site, the two single-sheaf complexes and their integer shifts are bounded complexes of flat sheaves, hence K-flat. Compute their derived tensor by total tensor, using the K-flat-single comparison for $L[m]\otimes^L_AL^\vee[0]$ (resp. $L^\vee[-m]\otimes^L_AL[0]$), and extract the remaining shift of the second factor by the derived tensor-shift isomorphism $t^2$, whose representatives on these flat-term K-flat complexes are the chain-level integer tensor-shift maps. The total complex $L[m]\otimes L^\vee[-m]$ is concentrated in degree zero with sole term $L\otimes L^\vee$; use the degree-zero evaluation already obtained. The reverse order has sole term $L^\vee\otimes L$, and use its ordinary evaluation. Thus both displayed derived arrows are isomorphisms. On a local basis each sends $(ae)\otimes(be^\vee)$, in its stated order, to $ab$, with inverse $a\mapsto(ae)\otimes e^\vee$ (and the reversed formula in the other order). Under $e'=ue$ the dual is $u^{-1}e^\vee$, so these formulas are unchanged. We specify the reverse arrow independently on its sole degree-zero term: applying the graded braiding instead would introduce $(-1)^m$. The two specified arrows are the shifts of the ordinary evaluations under the total-shift normalization on original degree-zero terms.

source.place: Tag 0FNH (item-shift-tensor) and item-flip-tensor-product; K-flat computation: sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat)

proof.text: Use the canonical derived tensor comparison for $V_T$, with the coefficient-unit comparison and signed shift compatibilities. Its representatives are ordinary pullback on the flat single complexes of Step 3. Under the dual-pullback isomorphism of Step 2, the pulled evaluation sends the pulled basis and pulled dual basis to $1$, exactly as target evaluation does. More explicitly, the ordinary tensor comparison takes $a\otimes(x\otimes\phi)$ to $(a\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes\phi)$, and both composites to the coefficient ring give $a\phi(x)$. This is the evaluation-normalization equation in the dual-pullback theorem. The canonical comparison commutes with each signed tensor shift and the unitors, so the same equation holds for shifts $m,-m$ and for the reverse order. Hence it identifies the particular evaluation arrows of Step 3, as required, rather than only the source and target objects.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), representative construction; sites-modules.tex Tag 0GMX; signed-shift compatibility as in more-algebra.tex Tag 0FNH

proof.text: For either site let $P$ be either of its two flat line sheaves. For every module sheaf $M$ in degree zero the K-flat-single calculation gives $P[s]\otimes_A^LM\cong(P\otimes_AM)[s]$. Its cohomology is zero outside degree $-s$. By the definitions of Tor interval this is amplitude $[-s,-s]$. Take $(P,s)=(L,m),(L^\vee,-m)$ and their comparison images. Their only cohomology sheaves are the constructible sheaves of Steps 1--2; therefore they are bounded constructible with the claimed intervals.

source.place: Tag 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat), single-flat-term calculation; Tor interval is tested on all module sheaves

proof.text:
The flat-single normalization on an arbitrary ringed site, followed by the derived tensor-shift comparison, gives for every complex $K$ and integer $r$ the formula
$$\mathcal H^r(K\otimes_A^LP[s])\cong\mathcal H^{r+s}(K)\otimes_AP.$$
It applies without a flat representative or any Tor condition on $K$. Consequently, if the cohomology of $K$ vanishes outside $[u,v]$, the cohomology after tensoring with $P[s]$ vanishes outside $[u-s,v-s]$. This proves the needed boundedness on both sites.

source.place: Flat-single total-tensor computation of Tag 06YQ; shift comparisons descend from more-algebra.tex Tag 0FNH

proof.text: On the etale site, apply the flat-constructible tensor theorem with each of $L,L^\vee$, already flat and constructible, to the bounded constructible $K$. Its cohomology formula gives constructibility, and extracting the shift reindexes the cohomology sheaves. On the pro-etale site apply the finite-tensor constructible-cohomology lemma to $K$ and either $V_TL[0]$ or $V_TL^\vee[0]$. Its hypotheses are precisely bounded constructibility at $A=A_{E,n}$ and invertibility of $\ell$ on $T$: the first is supplied by Step 2 and the assumption on $K$, and the second follows since $T$ is over the field of characteristic different from $\ell$. It supplies constructible cohomology in every degree, with no absolute separatedness requirement. Extracting the shift again just reindexes. Combine with Step 6 for bounded constructibility.

source.place: Tag 095I (lemma-tensor-product-constructible), Tag 0961 (lemma-tensor-c); pro-etale local tensor calculation: sites-cohomology.tex Tag 094H

proof.text:
Finally let $K$ have Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ and let $M$ be any module sheaf in degree zero on the same site. The associator and symmetry of the symmetric monoidal derived category of the ringed site identify
$$(K\otimes_A^LP[s])\otimes_A^LM\cong(K\otimes_A^LM)\otimes_A^LP[s].$$
These constraints are induced by unsigned reassociation and the signed swap $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$ on total tensors of K-flat representatives, and the ringed-topos comparison statement describes the same constraints; no boundedness of the test module and no constructibility of it are assumed. Apply Step 6 to the complex $K\otimes_A^LM$: by the Tor hypothesis its cohomology vanishes outside $[a,b]$, so the right side vanishes outside $[a-s,b-s]$. Since this works for every $M$, the definitions give the desired Tor interval. Substituting $s=m$ and $s=-m$ gives $[a-m,b-m]$ and $[a+m,b+m]$. Step 7 gives the remaining bounded-constructible condition, hence these tensors lie in $D^b_{ctf}$ as asserted.
